method_limits: the follow is one name wide: `p = join(...)` then `q = p` then open(q) reads as `flows_into_another_call`-free (p is only assigned to q, classed as a non-consuming use), so aliasing through a second name is not followed and a dropped site can be a missed consumer rather than a missing one

the read test is by name inside the scope, not by position: a read that appears before the assignment on the same name (a loop variable, a previous binding) counts and is disclosed by `name_rebound_in_scope` instead of being resolved

a composition is recognised by the dotted tail `path.join` (or a bare `join`) and by a *Path / *path constructor on the left of a division; `obj.join(a, b)` on some other receiver is not in the population, so this face bounds `path.join` sites only
Path division is recognised when the left operand is a *Path constructor or another division; `p / 'x'` where p is a name bound earlier is not in this population
scope is the nearest def/class-free body; a name read only inside a nested def counts as a closure capture and is published in its own class rather than as a consumer
static only: nothing is executed, so a path handed to a function that opens it somewhere else is `flows_into_another_call`, not `consumed`
